incident.title: Checkout latency surge across EU region
incident.description: Checkout p95 latency climbed from 420 ms to 8.4 s shortly after the payment-router deployment. Error rate is 18% in eu-central and the retry queue continues to grow.

agents.name: Incident Commander
agents.mission: Maintain global incident state, coordinate team leads, and enforce the human approval boundary.

agents.name: Triage Orchestrator
agents.mission: Establish severity, scope, customer impact, and the first causal hypotheses.
agents.outputSummary: Scope confirmed; focused incident response is warranted

agents.name: Alert Correlator
agents.mission: Cluster related alerts and establish a reliable incident onset window.
agents.outputSummary: Three alert families share a single onset window

agents.name: Impact Analyst
agents.mission: Quantify affected journeys, regions, and customer cohorts.
agents.outputSummary: Customer checkout completion is materially degraded

agents.name: Change Intelligence
agents.mission: Correlate deployments, configuration changes, and feature flags with incident onset.
agents.outputSummary: Incident onset strongly correlates with the latest router release

agents.name: Investigation Orchestrator
agents.mission: Direct evidence gathering and converge on the most defensible causal hypothesis.
agents.outputSummary: Evidence converges on a connection lifecycle regression

agents.name: Telemetry Analyst
agents.mission: Analyze golden signals, saturation, and regional metric divergence.
agents.outputSummary: Connection-pool saturation is driving latency amplification

agents.name: Log Investigator
agents.mission: Extract high-value error patterns and trace them to code or configuration paths.
agents.outputSummary: New routing branch leaks gateway connections on timeout

agents.name: Dependency Mapper
agents.mission: Map upstream and downstream health to isolate the failing boundary.
agents.outputSummary: External payment gateway is healthy; failure is at the client boundary

agents.name: Response Orchestrator
agents.mission: Build a reversible mitigation plan and coordinate recovery after approval.
agents.outputSummary: Canary a rollback of payment-router in eu-central, expand only after golden signals recover, then drain queued retries at a controlled rate.

agents.name: Mitigation Strategist
agents.mission: Rank the fastest safe options for stopping customer impact.
agents.outputSummary: A regional rollback is the fastest bounded mitigation

agents.name: Risk & Rollback Reviewer
agents.mission: Challenge the proposed mitigation and define explicit rollback triggers.
agents.outputSummary: Rollback risk is lower than continued customer impact

agents.name: Recovery Verifier
agents.mission: Independently verify service recovery against predeclared checks.

agents.name: Communications Orchestrator
agents.mission: Keep a live record and deliver accurate, audience-specific updates.
agents.outputSummary: Incident record and stakeholder narrative are current

agents.name: Incident Scribe
agents.mission: Maintain a factual, timestamped incident timeline and decision log.
agents.outputSummary: Incident timeline and decision ledger are synchronized

agents.name: Stakeholder Liaison
agents.mission: Draft concise updates without leaking unverified technical claims.
agents.outputSummary: Stakeholder update is ready for release

agents.name: Postmortem Analyst
agents.mission: Create a blameless causal summary and concrete follow-up actions.

findings.headline: Three alert families share a single onset window
findings.detail: Latency, HTTP error, and queue-depth alerts for payment-router all changed within the same two-minute window, indicating one incident rather than independent failures.
evidence: First sustained breach observed in eu-central
p95 latency 8.4 s (baseline 420 ms)
HTTP 5xx rate 18%

findings.headline: Customer checkout completion is materially degraded
findings.detail: The eu-central checkout path is the primary affected journey. Elevated latency and retries imply both failed purchases and duplicate-attempt risk, supporting SEV-1 handling.
evidence: Scope is concentrated in eu-central
Estimated checkout completion is 31% below the normal band
Other regions remain inside their error-budget burn thresholds

findings.headline: Incident onset strongly correlates with the latest router release
findings.detail: Release 2026.08.25.3 of payment-router reached eu-central six minutes before the first alert. No concurrent database or gateway configuration change was recorded.
evidence: Release 2026.08.25.3 completed at 14:26 UTC
First alert fired at 14:32 UTC
Previous release has a known-good 24-hour baseline

findings.headline: Connection-pool saturation is driving latency amplification
findings.detail: payment-router instances in eu-central show pool utilization pinned above 97% while CPU and memory remain normal. Retry amplification explains the rising queue depth.
evidence: Gateway connection pool: 97-100% utilized
Application CPU: 41%; memory: 58%
Retry attempts per checkout increased from 1.1 to 3.8

findings.headline: New routing branch leaks gateway connections on timeout
findings.detail: Logs from payment-router repeatedly pair upstream timeout messages with missing connection-release markers on the new v3 routing branch. The legacy branch closes connections correctly.
evidence: PAYMENT_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT increased 22x after deployment
releaseConnection marker absent on the v3 timeout path
Legacy v2 path retains a balanced acquire/release ratio

findings.headline: External payment gateway is healthy; failure is at the client boundary
findings.detail: The upstream gateway, checkout API, and database are healthy outside calls made by payment-router. The fault boundary is the router's connection lifecycle in eu-central.
evidence: Gateway synthetic probes remain below 180 ms
Database query p95 remains below 24 ms
Only v3 router instances show elevated open connections

findings.headline: A regional rollback is the fastest bounded mitigation
findings.detail: Rolling payment-router in eu-central back to the previous release removes the suspected path while containing change to the affected region. Queue recovery should wait for latency stabilization.
evidence: Previous release artifact passed current smoke tests
Regional deployment supports one-click rollback
Traffic shifting alone would move retry pressure downstream

findings.headline: Rollback risk is lower than continued customer impact
findings.detail: The previous release is schema-compatible and the rollout can be stopped after the first canary. The main secondary risk is replaying the payment retry queue too quickly.
evidence: No database migration accompanied the release
Rollback canary limits initial exposure to 5% of instances
Queue drain supports a configurable transactions-per-second cap

findings.headline: Incident timeline and decision ledger are synchronized
findings.detail: The live record now captures alert onset, payment-router deployment timing, hypotheses, evidence, and the approval boundary. Unverified claims are labeled as hypotheses.

plan.hypothesis: Release 2026.08.25.3 introduced a missing connection-release path after upstream timeouts, saturating the regional gateway pool and amplifying retries.
plan.summary: Canary a rollback of payment-router in eu-central, expand only after golden signals recover, then drain queued retries at a controlled rate.
plan.blastRadius: Only payment-router instances in eu-central; start with a 5% canary.

actions.title: Freeze regional changes and preserve evidence
actions.detail: Pause unrelated deployments in the affected region and capture current release, metric, and error-pattern references.
actions.expectedSignal: No additional configuration drift during mitigation

actions.title: Canary rollback to release 2026.08.24.7
actions.detail: Roll back 5% of regional instances, observe for five minutes, and expand only if latency and pool saturation improve.
actions.expectedSignal: p95 latency below 800 ms and pool utilization below 70%

actions.title: Drain the payment retry queue
actions.detail: After service metrics stabilize, replay queued work at 20% of normal throughput with duplicate-payment protection enabled.
actions.expectedSignal: Queue depth declines without renewed latency or duplicate attempts

plan.rollback: Stop expansion immediately if canary error rate exceeds 2%, restore release 2026.08.25.3, and isolate the region behind the existing traffic-shift control.
validationChecks: Checkout p95 latency remains below 800 ms for ten minutes
Retry queue declines monotonically without duplicate-payment alerts
